title: a crossfade read a fixed partition length regardless of the input frame's sample count
object: an audio plane of the input frame, from av_frame_get_buffer
lifetime_ender: NONE -- the buffer is alive throughout. SPATIAL row.
shape: a fixed-length read from a frame whose final partition is shorter
allocator_layer: the platform allocator itself: one direct av_malloc-family allocation, no inner layer. FFmpeg's av_malloc is malloc plus alignment.
fidelity: model consumer, real arithmetic: the sizes and the crossing expression are upstream's, quoted in PROVENANCE.md.
live_proof: absent at the pin: n9.0.1:libavfilter/afir_template.c computes `const int nb_samples = FFMIN(min_part_size, s->in->nb_samples - offset);` and copies that. The unclamped `min_part_size` form is at 3fbb9560821b^ and is absent from the pin.

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: PREDICTED, not measured. The request is exactly a jemalloc size class, so the usable size equals the requested size and there is no slack to absorb the crossing -- confirmed by tools/size-class-audit.py, which reports `faults` for this case. The capability's bounds end where the allocation does and the probe SHOULD fault.

status: built 2026-10-08; native arms measured by runners/run-native.sh in the same commit. The platform arms are declared predictions.
nested_why: the crossed buffer came straight from av_malloc / av_mallocz / av_calloc / av_malloc_array -- which on the platform is malloc -- with no AVBufferPool or AVRefStructPool between it and the request. So under this inventory's axis, WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT, this row is NOT nested.
distinguishing: the length is a CONFIGURATION constant -- the minimum partition size -- rather than anything derived from the data, so the crossing appears only on the final partition of a frame and scales with how short that partition is. The fix introduces a clamped nb_samples, which is also why the same commit touches a sibling expression in fir_quantum.
